title: Backtesting and Forward Testing
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/0/bod: A **backtest** means running your system's rules on past data to see what results they would have given. In a **manual backtest**, you move the chart forward candle by candle (for example with TradingView's **Bar Replay**) and log every trade in a spreadsheet.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/1/bod: Record the same details for every trade so you can later work out **win rate, expectancy and drawdown**. Log results in **R** so the account size doesn't matter.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/2/pro: Put the steps of a manual backtest in order.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/2/ite: Write down the system's exact rules
Pick the market and test period
Move the chart forward candle by candle
Log every trade in the spreadsheet
Calculate win rate, expectancy and drawdown
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/2/exp: Without written rules, a backtest turns into in-the-moment judgment calls. And the stats only mean something once every trade is logged.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/3/pro: Why do you hide future candles in a manual backtest?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/3/opt: So knowing what comes next doesn't sway your decisions
So the losing trades stay hidden
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/3/exp: When you can see what comes next, you subconsciously “miss” the bad entries and take the good ones. A backtest like that comes out better than reality.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/4/pro: Rule: “Buy on the first candle that closes above the SMA 10 (the gold line).” You've moved the chart forward candle by candle. Tap the entry candle.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/4/exp: Before this candle, every close was below the average. This is the first candle whose body closed above the SMA 10, so by the rule, this is the entry.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/5/sta: 10 to 20 trades are enough to judge a system.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/5/exp: In a small sample, luck drives the result. Many traders want at least about 100 trades, across different market conditions, before they judge.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/6/bod: The more trades, the more reliable the stats. At least **100 trades** is the usual advice. Even more important, the test should cover **different conditions**: trending, ranging, high and low volatility.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/6/tip: A system tested in only one kind of market hasn't passed its exam yet.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/7/pro: The results of 10 backtest trades in R were: +2, −1, −1, +2, −1, +2, −1, −1, +2, −1. What's the expectancy per trade?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/7/exp: Total: 4 × 2 − 6 × 1 = +2R over 10 trades, which is +0.2R per trade. Of course, 10 trades is far too few to trust that number.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/8/pro: Your backtest only covered one 3-month period with a strong uptrend, and the results are great. What's the main problem?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/8/opt: The system wasn't tested in ranges or downtrends
Three months is too long for any backtest
No problem; great results are enough
lessons/trading-system-u3-l1/steps/8/exp: Good results in one kind of market might only mean “buying worked in an uptrend”. Before you trust it, test the system in other conditions too.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/0/bod: **Overfitting** means tuning your rules and parameters to past data so much that the system memorizes the past's **noise** instead of a real pattern. The result: a great backtest and weak live trading.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/1/bod: **Way too many** rules and parameters, **oddly precise** numbers (like SMA 37 and RSI 23), an equity curve that's **too smooth**, and results that **fall apart** with one small parameter change.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/1/tip: A robust system works about the same with nearby parameters (say SMA 35 to 40).
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/2/sta: If SMA 37 works great but SMA 35 and SMA 40 lose money, that's a sign of overfitting.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/2/exp: Real market patterns aren't that sensitive to one specific number. When only one number works, the system has probably memorized past coincidences.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/3/bod: **Look-ahead bias** means your test uses information that wasn't available at that moment, like entering at a candle's **open** based on that same candle's **close**. **Survivorship bias** means testing only on assets that have **survived** to today.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/4/opt: Entering at a candle's open based on that same candle's close
Entering at the next candle's open after the signal candle closes
Using a fixed stop loss for every trade
Subtracting spread and commission from results
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/4/exp: When a candle opens, you don't know yet where it'll close. The second option is the right way: wait for the signal candle to close, then enter on the next one.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/5/pro: Someone tested their strategy over the last 5 years on the 20 coins with the biggest market cap today. What bias is their result likely to have?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/5/exp: Coins that mattered 5 years ago and then crashed or got delisted aren't on this list. Testing only on “today's winners” paints the past too rosy.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/6/bod: One way to fight it: **split your data**. For example, use the first 70% to build and tune the system, and **don't touch** the last 30% until the very end, then test on it. If results are much worse on the untouched data, you're probably overfitting.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/7/pro: You have 5 years of data. You use the first 70% to build the system and set aside the last 30% for out-of-sample testing. How long is the out-of-sample period?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/7/exp: 30% of 5 years = 1.5 years. The first 3.5 years are for building and tuning the system.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/8/pai: Memorizing the noise in past data
Using information that didn't exist yet
Testing only on assets that are still around
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/9/pro: Compare these four systems. Which is most reliable?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/9/opt: 3 simple rules that are also positive out of sample
12 rules with precise parameters, great only on build data
A perfectly smooth curve with zero drawdown over 20 trades
A result that turns negative when SMA goes from 20 to 22
lessons/trading-system-u3-l2/steps/9/exp: Simplicity and success on untouched data are two big signs of robustness. The other options show classic signs of overfitting or too small a sample.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/0/bod: A **forward test** means running your system in real time, without seeing the future, on a **demo account** or with very small size. It tests things a backtest can't show: **your own execution**, costs and **slippage**.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/1/bod: Compare your forward results with the backtest. Being a little weaker is **normal**. But if it's **much worse** after enough trades, the backtest's edge probably came from overfitting or costs you didn't count.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/2/pro: Put a system's path from idea to live account in order.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/2/ite: Forward test on a demo account
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/2/exp: Each stage is a new filter: a system that fails one doesn't move on to the next. Real money comes in last, and with low risk.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/3/pro: Your backtest without costs showed: 50% win rate, 12-pip average win and 10-pip average loss. If each trade costs 1.5 pips (spread and commission), what's the real expectancy per trade?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/3/exp: Before costs: 0.5 × 12 − 0.5 × 10 = +1 pip. Costs come off every trade: 1 − 1.5 = −0.5 pips. A system that was profitable on paper loses money once costs are in.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/4/sta: Demo account results are always exactly the same as a live account's.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/4/exp: On a live account, slippage and how orders get filled can differ, and most importantly, real fear and greed come into play. That's why traders start small even after a demo.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/5/pro: After 25 trades, your forward test is a little weaker than the backtest but still positive. What's the most sensible move?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/5/opt: Keep testing until the sample is bigger
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/5/exp: 25 trades is too few to judge, and a small dip from the backtest is natural. Rushing to change parameters is itself a path to overfitting.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/6/sen: After a successful forward test, start your live account with ___ risk and raise it ___.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/6/exp: Your first months live test your execution under real pressure. Low risk means the mistakes of this period stay cheap.
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/7/pai: The gap between buy and sell price
The gap between requested and filled price
Cost or credit for holding overnight
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/8/pro: Put all the stages together. What's the sensible next step?
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/8/opt: Go live with low risk, like 0.5%
Drop the system because the number shrank
lessons/trading-system-u3-l3/steps/8/exp: Results stayed positive and close together across all three stages, and a small dip is natural. Now it's time for real money, but with low risk, so your own execution under pressure gets confirmed too.
